To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Polish local government system is three-levelled (gmina, powiat and województwo) and this three-tiered structure provides a basis for analysing cooperation between local government units, both in the horizontal (between units at the same level) and vertical (between units of different levels) dimensions;

the Polish local government system is characterized by the following features: (1) a three-tier structure (municipal, county and regional), (2) a high degree of autonomy of the local authorities, and (3) a high degree and variety of cooperation between them.

the cooperation of local government units in Poland is a complex phenomenon, and the forms of cooperation can be divided into two groups: public law forms (e.g. intermunicipal unions, agreements, and associations of municipalities, counties and voivodships) and private law forms (e. g. joint-stock companies, limited partnerships, limited liability partnerships).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of cooperation between the territorial self-governing bodies in Poland.
the cooperation of local self-governments (LSG) in Poland (the local government structures) and the forms and the legal basis of this cooperation.
the analysis of the legal basis and the forms of cooperation between local government units in Poland, with particular emphasis on the forms of public law.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cooperation of local self-government units in Poland (the structures of local self-government) is based on the Constitution and the European Charter of Local Self-Government.
The structure of the Polish local government (municipal, powiat, and regional self-government) forms the basis for analysing the cooperation between local government entities.

the Polish territorial self-governing system is three-tiered (the commune, powiat and the voivodship level), which makes it possible to analyse the co-operation of self-governing bodies both in the horizontal dimension (i.e. between bodies on the same level) and the vertical dimension (i.e., between bodies of different levels).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Polish system of local authorities is based on three-tier structure (gmina, powiat, and województwo), which is a basis for the analysis of cooperation between local authorities, both horizontally between units of the same level and vertically between units of different levels.
the Polish system of local government is based on three levels: local (commune), intermediate (powiat) and regional (voivodeship).

the three-tier structure of Polish territorial self-government (municipal, county and voivodeship self-government) is the basis for analyzing the cooperation of territorial self-government bodies both in the horizontal dimension between units of the same level, and in the vertical dimension between units of different levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Polish local government system is based on the principle of subsidiarity, and the principle of local autonomy.
there are many forms of cooperation between the territorial self-government units in Poland.
the Polish local government is a three-tiered structure. It includes the local, county and regional levels.
